text:
maya: quick heads-up — after enabling NF4 (canary 20%) for the 13B family we saw a reproducible throughput drop (~20%) and GPU memory jump on several nodes. pods on p4d-8x were fine but p3x16/RTX A6000 showed memory spike + one OOM.
jon: saw this in the metrics dashboard. tokens/s per replica down from ~4200 -> ~3300, latency p50 up ~12%. perf-bot uploaded a flamegraph: kernel selection shifted to a slow INT4 fallback for attention on long sequences.
maya: exact repro: curl to our canary endpoint with seq_len ~1024 and batch 4. attaching the minimal script.
maya: ```bash
for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"<long prompt...>","max_tokens":512}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate; done
```
ryan: ran a local trace with `nsys` — the NVTX spans show repeated kernel swap at the start of decode where kernel_selector chooses the NF4 kernel but then falls back to a generic FP32 path when calibration mismatch occurs. That fallback allocates a temp buffer each time, causing fragmentation.
anita: can you paste the kernel_selector logs? I want to see the reason code for fallback.
jon: logs snippet:
jon: ```
[kernel_selector] choose_kernel: candidate=quant_nf4.attn_v2 score=0.78
[kernel_selector] calibrate_check: mismatch_scale=1.9 -> fallback to generic.attn
[kernel_selector] fallback_reason=calib_range_out_of_bounds
```
lex: that `mismatch_scale` looks like our histogram-based calibration failing for long tails. We recently tightened the calibration acceptance threshold in the last rollout (0.5 -> 0.25) to prevent quality regressions — might be too strict for this workload.
maya: interesting — if threshold is too strict, selector might pick a safer generic kernel more often, which is slower and allocates larger temporary buffers. explains both throughput and mem.
ryan: confirmed with a quick patch: relaxing threshold back to 0.5 on canary nodes returned tokens/s to previous levels and memory stabilized. No quality regressions seen on the small eval set.
anita: we should avoid a full rollback. Proposal:
anita: 1) revert calibration threshold to 0.5 for canary and monitor
anita: 2) add a histogram tail guard in calibration to ignore rare outliers
anita: 3) add a kernel_selector metric for fallback_reason to alert earlier
jon: also suggest a batching heuristic change: for seq_len > 900 we currently pack into batches of 4 which amplifies the calibration mismatch; adding a per-route max_batch for long seq routes might help.
lex: agree. config snippet for quick patch:
lex: ```yaml
kernel_selector:
  quant_calib_threshold: 0.5
  ignore_percentile_tail: 0.999
routes:
  long_seq_route:
    max_batch: 2
```
maya: perf-bot shows GPU mem before/after patch: pre-patch RMS ~13GB -> post-patch ~9GB on the same workload.
deploy-bot: rolled patch kernel_selector:quant_calib_threshold=0.5 to canary (20%) at 1847654360 — monitors enabled.
jon: current canary stats (5m): throughput delta -2% (within noise), p95 latency back to baseline, no new OOMs.
ryan: I'll run a longer stress + full eval set overnight and post results.
anita: action items: @ryan run stress+eval, @lex add fallback_reason metric (simple counter), @maya coordinate canary ramp to 50% if overnight checks good. I'll draft a follow-up incident note if anything changes.
maya: thanks all — great catch. tagging perf-bot logs id perf-1847654321
perf-bot: perf-report uploaded: s3://perf-uploads/1847654321/trace-flame.svg
maya: closing loop: if any of you see other kernel-related regressions, please ping eng-runtime. will update product on customer impact in the afternoon.
